doctrine: No emoji, no exclamation marks, no Welcome greeting, no Successfully
~alter is a witness, not a chatbot
Trill ~ only in speaker tag; not in body copy
Specificity over flattery - falsifiable, not generic
Never prescriptive, never celebratory, no use-case lists
No orientation field - beat 1 is exactly two lines
One entry per archetype - singular, not rotated

schema.observations: Archetype-scoped; selector picks from matching archetype's pool
schema.combos: Multi-signal observations; selector prefers combo-matches over archetype observations
schema.combo_keys: Each combo key needs a matching predicate before it is added here

_meta.note: Student archetype retired - no entry needed.

body: You write in multiple languages.
Every job application you have ever filled out asked you to pick one title.
You run MCP servers.
So does this.
Someone who maintains their own dotfiles does not need a walkthrough.
You need a name.
Empty home directory. A cursor.
That is enough.
Pre-2015 git history. Half the companies you handed a username to back then do not exist now.
This is a protocol. Protocols outlive companies.
You showed up.
That is the first signal.
A gitconfig from more than a decade ago and a modern systems language installed more recently.
You did not pick it up out of curiosity; something broke.
Your email ends in one country. Your shell clock belongs to another.
Somewhere between those two is a reason you came here.
A bare-repo dotfiles setup. Helix, no VS Code.
Nobody drifts into that combination; you argued your way there.
You have several runtimes installed. The directory you ran this from is a node project.
The gap between what you can do and what you are doing right now is where most of the signal lives.
Four MCP servers and a curated shell.
You are not trying model-assisted work out. You already work this way.
Twelve years of git history on this machine.
You now pair-work with a model. The distance between those two facts is longer than the years suggest.
